full_judgment: 4. A similar question came up before this Court in a subsequent case, Hazi Tozammbar Ali vs. Abdus Sailor, 34 DLR (AD) 217. Three of the Judges of this Court were common to the decisions in both the cases, one in 32 DLR (AD) 54 and the other in 34 DLR (AD) 217. In the latter, the lands transferred consisted of seven plots, all recorded under a single khatian and the pre-emptor's land was contiguous to two of those seven plots, but nevertheless, he was held to be owning land "contiguous to the land transferred", because though the pre-emptor's land was contiguous to two of the seven plots transferred, but all those seven plots were not only contiguous to each other but they together constituted one single block of land; as such the entire block was treated as contiguous to the land of the pre-emptor. In that connection the policy behind allowing pre-emption to a contiguous land-holder was explained and it was observed that one of the purposes for allowing pre-emption to a contiguous land-holder was apparently to help enlarge small uneconomical agricultural holdings by consolidation or amalgamation.
